note: k as in ကား (ká) "car". The first letter of the alphabet.
The breathy partner of က: same k, plus a puff of air. Starts ခုနစ် (hkṵn-hniʔ) 'seven'.
g. Voiced partner in the throat row. The ဂ in မင်္ဂလာပါ (mìn-gə-là-bà).
The nasal of the throat row: 'ng' at the start of a word, as in ငါး (ngá) 'five'.
s as in စား (sá) 'eat'.
The breathy partner of စ: s with a puff of air.
z as in ကျေးဇူး (kyéi-zú), the 'thank' in thank you.
The nasal of the palate row: 'ny'. Ends နာမည် (nàn-mè) 'name'.
t as in တယ် (dè), the statement ending you hear constantly.
The breathy partner of တ. Starts ထမင်း (htə-mín) 'rice'.
d as in ဒါ (dà) 'this'.
The nasal of the teeth row. Starts နေကောင်းလား (nèi káun lá) 'how are you?'.
p as in ပါ (bà), the politeness word you put almost everywhere.
The breathy partner of ပ. Starts ဖြည်းဖြည်း (hpyé-hpyé) 'slowly'.
b. The less common of the two b-letters.
Also b, and the common one: ဘာ (bà) 'what?'. Same sound as ဗ.
The nasal of the lips row. Starts မင်္ဂလာပါ (mìn-gə-là-bà) 'hello'.
y. Hides in တယ် (dè), the statement ending.
Spelled 'r' but said 'y' in Yangon: ရေ (yèi) 'water'.
l as in လား (lá), the yes/no question word.
A plain circle: w for wheel. Starts ဝမ်းသာ (wún-thà) 'glad'.
th, as in သွား (thwá) 'go'.
h, as in ဟုတ်ကဲ့ (houʔ kḛ) 'yes'.
No consonant sound: it carries a vowel on its own. Starts အမေ (ə-mèi) 'mother'.
A long 'a', relaxed and level (low tone).
Two dots (း) sit up high, so: HIGH tone. ကား also means 'car'.
Same sound as ာ. The tall form is used after round letters like ပ ဂ ဒ ဝ ခ င, so they don't look like other letters.
A small circle on top: a short, creaky 'i'.
Filled-in circle on top: a long 'i', low tone.
Add the two high dots (း) and the tone goes high.
One hook below: a short, creaky 'u'.
Two hooks below: a long 'u', low tone.
Long u with the high dots: high tone.
The trick: ေ is WRITTEN BEFORE the consonant but SAID AFTER it. ကေ = k + ei.
Same written-first ေ, plus the high dots.
This vowel is high tone on its own, no dots needed.
A dot below (့) squeezes the sound: creaky tone. As in ဟုတ်ကဲ့ (houʔ kḛ) 'yes'.
Vowels combine like Lego: ေ in front + ာ behind = 'aw'. High tone.
Add ် on top and the aw becomes low tone.
More Lego: circle on top + hook below = 'o'.
ကိုး (kó) is also 'nine'.
The mark ် 'kills' the letter's vowel. Any stop letter at the end (က် တ် ပ် စ်) = a sharp cut-off: checked tone.
Different letter, same result: a short, sharply stopped syllable.
You don't actually say the p: it just stops the sound.
Nasal letters at the end (င် န် မ်) make the vowel nasal instead of stopping it.
The n isn't really pronounced: the vowel goes nasal.
Spelled with m, sounds the same as န်.
The hook ျ hanging on the right adds a 'y': k + y = ky.
The bracket ြ wraps around the letter. Spelled 'r', but in Yangon it's said like ျ: ky.
The little loop below adds a 'w': k + w = kw.
The tail ှ makes a nasal breathy: breathe out through your nose before m. As in နှစ် (hniʔ) 'two'.
